## UI Design Phase — Complete ✅

### Design Direction
Dark navy base (`#0F0F1A`) + rose-coral gradient accent (`#FF4458 → #FF6B35`), system fonts only, zero external dependencies. Two viewport contexts: 390 px phone frames for auth/onboarding, 820–960 px browser frames for tablet-adaptive flows.

### Key Design Decisions

- **Screen 01** — "Dating without the download" tagline is prominent in the hero. The PWA install banner is placed *below* the form so it doesn't interrupt auth — but it's always visible as a secondary CTA.

- **Screen 02** — This flow has friction at the photo upload step, so the design provides three parallel paths (camera, file picker, drag-to-reorder) plus social-proof copy to drive completion. The 3×2 grid with a double-height primary slot teaches users which photo matters most without instruction text.

- **Screen 03** — Users will expect swipe cards to work exactly like mobile. The tablet layout moves action buttons into a sidebar column so nothing requires scrolling at 820 px. Keyboard shortcuts (← → ↑) are surfaced inline — a genuine web-native advantage competitors lack.

- **Screen 04** — To make this more intuitive on tablet, the two-panel layout follows the PRD spec exactly: conversation list left at 290 px, active thread right. The new-matches strip at the top of the left panel keeps the match discovery loop visible even while chatting.

- **Screen 05** — The install prompt uses a bottom sheet pattern (matching Chrome's native UI) over a blurred app shell so users understand *what* they're installing before accepting. The offline shell shows cached content rather than a blank screen — the single biggest UX differentiator over every competitor named in the Market Analysis.
